title: Google's Big Sleep agent may have isolated SQLite CVE-2025–6965 from threat-intel artifacts; fixed in 3.50.2 before exploitation
summary: Google says Big Sleep, fed indicators that attackers were staging a zero-day, isolated SQLite CVE-2025–6965; SQLite shipped the fix in 3.50.2 on 28 June 2025, announced 15 July 2025.
account: The SQLite 3.50.2 release carrying the fix is dated 28 June 2025. The CVE record was published 15 July 2025. Google's post says that, based on intel from Google Threat Intelligence, the Big Sleep agent discovered an SQLite vulnerability known only to threat actors. It was at risk of being exploited, the post says. A Google spokesperson told The Record that its threat intelligence group found artifacts indicating a zero-day was being staged but could not identify the vulnerability. Big Sleep was used to isolate it, the spokesperson said. Google declined to name the actors or describe the indicators. The CVE record, assigned by Google, credits Vlad Stolyarov of Google's Threat Analysis Group with assistance from Google Big Sleep. SQLite's release log lists the corresponding fix. Independent confirmation that exploitation was imminent is absent. The claim rests on Google.
purpose: Actively search for and find unknown security vulnerabilities in software using a large language model (LLM) agent (Google DeepMind and Project Zero).
deployer: Google (Threat Analysis Group / Big Sleep team)

ratings.reason: SQLite fixed the flaw in 3.50.2 (release log entry on aggregate terms exceeding column count) before public exploitation was reported.
No source documents an outcome for users beyond the patch. The foiled-exploitation claim is Google's.

ai_role.statement: Per Google's spokesperson, human threat analysts supplied limited indicators and Big Sleep isolated the specific vulnerability. The CVE credit names a human finder “with assistance from Google Big Sleep”. Developer and the organization reporting the benefit are the same company. The Record and the SQLite release log are the independent sources. Neither confirms the threat-actor staging.

fields.account: The SQLite 3.50.2 release carrying the fix is dated 28 June 2025. The CVE record was published 15 July 2025. Google's post says that, based on intel from Google Threat Intelligence, the Big Sleep agent discovered an SQLite vulnerability known only to threat actors. It was at risk of being exploited, the post says. A Google spokesperson told The Record that its threat intelligence group found artifacts indicating a zero-day was being staged but could not identify the vulnerability. Big Sleep was used to isolate it, the spokesperson said. Google declined to name the actors or describe the indicators. The CVE record, assigned by Google, credits Vlad Stolyarov of Google's Threat Analysis Group with assistance from Google Big Sleep. SQLite's release log lists the corresponding fix. Independent confirmation that exploitation was imminent is absent. The claim rests on Google.
